geographyNote: City of Richmond, British Columbia (census subdivision)

facts.text: Vancouver International Airport, located in Richmond, welcomed more than 26.9 million travellers in 2025, an all-time record, with cargo also at its highest volume in the airport's 94-year history.
YVR supports more than 26,500 jobs on Sea Island in Richmond, making the airport a major employment hub for the region.
Over 14,500 Richmond businesses support around 125,000 jobs, a six percent increase, and the city's economy has remained relatively robust and stable compared with the slower BC economy.
The City of Richmond is developing a new Economic Development Strategy to guide its long-term economic direction, support business growth and retention, and strengthen community resilience.
Richmond has established strengths in logistics and transportation, thanks to its proximity to Vancouver International Airport and the Port of Vancouver, plus emerging strength in clean technology.

overview: Richmond had 209,937 residents in the 2021 Census, up 5.9 percent from 198,309 in 2016, spread over 128.87 square kilometres of islands in the Fraser delta. Its 81,080 occupied dwellings house a highly multicultural population, and the median household income was $79,000 in 2020, a little below neighbouring suburbs.

The airport is the economic engine, supporting tens of thousands of jobs on Sea Island, while logistics, technology and a large Asian-Canadian business community round out the picture. For a local business, Richmond rewards multilingual marketing and a presence in City Centre or Steveston, where customers are concentrated.

byService.lead-generation: In Richmond, lead generation should combine Chinese-language and English campaigns aimed at City Centre and Steveston households, plus business-to-business outreach to the airport and logistics firms on Sea Island.

byService.branding: With a median household income of $79,000 and a strong trading heritage, Richmond branding should feel international and trustworthy, using visuals that respect the city's diverse communities.
